conditions: Real-valued random variable X has finite support consisting of the distinct listed real values x_i, i=1,...,n, with n a positive integer.
spoken_aliases: the expected value of random variable x equals the sum from i equals one to n of x sub i times the probability that random variable x equals x sub i
expectation of x equals the sum from i equals one to n of the product of x sub i and the probability that x equals x sub i

evidence: For a finite real-valued random variable, partition the probability space into the disjoint events X=x_i. Integrating X over each event gives x_i P(X=x_i); summing yields the expectation. Finiteness ensures all terms and the mean are finite.

Reference cross-check: https://openstax.org/books/introductory-statistics-2e/pages/4-2-mean-or-expected-value-and-standard-deviation. Checked 2026-11-27. Proposed maintainer approval; not independent human certification.
